findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the failure to use a barrier to shut off the faucet at the handwashing sink by staffers. PIC was made aware of the behavior and PIC educated staffers on proper handwashing procedures. Ensure that staff are aware of the proper handwashing procedures to avoid recontaminating their hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The build up of soil was observed in multiple nozzles on the Coca-Cola soda machine and the tea dispenser in the lobby. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that the nozzles as well as the tea dispensers nozzles are going to get cleaned. Ensure that food-contact surfaces such as the soda machine and the tea dispenser nozzles are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Visible light was observed coming from the back exit door of the facility. PIC was made aware that such gaps provide entry for insects, rodents, and other pest into the facility. PIC ensured inspector that the relevant repairs would be done to seal the opening. Ensure that the mentioned gaps in the door are sealed to allow the door to fully sealed when closed in order to discourage the entry of pests in the facility.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Accumulated ice was observed on the floor and behind the fan unit in the walk-in freezer. PIC was made aware of the accumulated ice in the above mentioned areas. Ensure that the accumulated ice is removed providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a pile of unused equipments being stored in the back of the dry storage area. Discussed with PIC and PIC mentioned that the pile of unused faulty equipments had been in that spot for a while  and was unsure about the next action towards them. Ensure that unnecessary items such as the pile of unused equipments are removed from the facility.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: The hand sink in the kitchen was observed with no paper towels at the start of the inspection. PIC placed a new roll of paper towels in the dispenser during the inspection. Ensure that a supply of paper towels is readily available at all times at the hand sink. 
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: The triple sink and the sanitizer buckets were recorded at 0ppm QUAT. There was observed no sanitizer hooked up to the dispenser. PIC was able to locate a bag of sanitizer in their storage closet and replaced this bag at the dispenser at the triple sink. The triple sink and the sanitizer buckets were tested at 400ppm QUAT after the bag was replaced. Ensure that sanitizer is replaced as soon as it is empty and that a ready supply is available in the facility and that test strips are utilized at least every 4 hours in the triple sink and the sanitizer bucket to ensure the sanitizer efficacy remains. 
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The soda nozzles at the drive thru are observed to have an accumulation on the plastic pieces, especially in the corners where the plastic lifts up. Ensure these nozzles are removed, scrubbed, and sanitized during the cleaning procedure. A follow-up is being scheduled for Monday, May 14th, 2024 to observe these items. 
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-205.15: The following plumbing systems are observed in disrepair:
-The hand sink is observed to not be able to be shut off completely.
-The triple sink is observed leaking at the left drain pipe.
Ensure corrections are made to these items by a licensed plumber. A follow-up is being scheduled for Monday, May 6, 2024 to observe the corrections that have been made. 
5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: There is observed a board above the mop sink that has exposed wood. Ensure this board is sealed with a layer of paint or other substance that makes it a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface. 
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: There is observed an accumulation of food debris/soils int he following locations:
-Below the bun toaster machine inside the door is a large accumulation of food debris/soils.
-Under the coffee station is observed an accumulation of liquid.
Ensure these locations are cleaned to remove the current accumulation of food debris/soils and then cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The walk-in freezer is observed to have an accumulation of ice on the piping. This ice needs to be removed and then the pipe needs to be repaired so that the ice accumulation does not form.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.
